title: We Were There
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Nanami 'Nana' Takahashi starts high school and falls for the popular Motoharu Yano, who still carries the loss of his older girlfriend, killed in a car accident the summer before. Their romance grows slowly around his grief, his distrust after being lied to, and her uncertainty; a later time skip follows them into adulthood (Manga Bookshelf; VIZ blurb via AniList; AniList Time Skip).
life_message: Love means honesty and patience with another person's grief, and first love shapes who we become.

content.note: A fatal car accident in the backstory (Manga Bookshelf); no fighting noted.
Grief and tragedy run through it: Manga Bookshelf on Yano's hidden pain; AniList Tragedy (77); MU Death of Loved One/s, Regret.
Romance is central; MU lists Sexual Coercion (to verify what is shown and how it is framed).
Grief, guilt and fear of abandonment (Manga Bookshelf; MU Depression, Guilt); MU and AniList (spoiler) tag Suicide (to verify how shown).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are inward and emotional, not about honor (Manga Bookshelf).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Teens make their own romantic choices with little adult direction.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Yano's family life and single parent shape the story (MU Single Parent, Family Drama).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Classmates and couples meet as equals; class-president duty is a minor burden.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Feelings and personal fulfilment in love are the main concern.

folkways.japan: School-year rituals, class-president duties and restrained expression of feelings reflect Japanese school culture.

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf praises its 'simplicity and quiet honesty' and finds no melodrama.

personified.ideology: Refuses comforting lies after being lied to

delivery.note: Its view of love and grief is left for readers to infer from small moments rather than stated.

winners_losers: No ideological sides; the story's sympathy lies with characters who face grief honestly, and its losses are personal (to verify the ending).
